topics.label: Course Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing for the lecture, introducing the lecturer, the course context, and the learning outcomes on cancer causes and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Fundamental Biology and Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and explain how intrinsic metabolic damage, DNA repair capacity, and inherited predispositions drive mutation accumulation.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss known environmental hazards, explore the debate between intrinsic bad luck and external exposures, and review geographical variations in cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections contribute to malignancy, featuring Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which radiation and dietary or chemical mutagens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on chronic inflammation, the two-stage initiation-promotion model, and host developmental vulnerability.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying and Assessing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review mutational signatures, biobanks, animal models, and in vitro assays used to evaluate carcinogenicity alongside the clinical and personal risk-benefit considerations.
